notes: 2021 Census housing and economic context for 29 BC census divisions. Income refers to 2020; housing and labour indicators retain their published reference periods and household or person universes.
Exact 2021 DGUID and native CD codes join Statistics Canada 2021 display polygons. No health-region conversion or population allocation is applied.
Owner and tenant percentages have separate denominators. Core housing need excludes ineligible households; the published non-farm, non-reserve private-household and 25% sample definitions apply.
Rounded Census counts, suppression symbols, data quality flags and long-form nonresponse rates are retained. Indigenous community values are not inferred from surrounding regional totals.
Percentages are percentage points. Income and dwelling values are nominal source dollars; rented shelter cost is CAD per month.

datasets.title: Northern municipal population estimates
datasets.description: Seven Northern municipalities, 2011–2025, extracted from the original BC Stats Mun-RD worksheet.
notes: Seven Northern municipalities, 2011–2025, extracted from the original BC Stats Mun-RD worksheet.

Population refers to July 1 each year. The source explicitly uses municipal boundaries as of July 1 of each stated year. The 2021 Census polygons provide display context; historical boundaries have not been harmonized.
Seven reviewed SGC-to-CSD code pairs preserve municipality identity. A municipality is distinct from its larger LHA or census agglomeration.
Prince George’s 2025 municipal estimate is 85,944; its larger LHA population is 105,544. These denominators cannot be substituted for one another.

datasets.title: Regional health-sector employment
datasets.description: Annual Labour Force Survey employment, 2020–2025, for seven BC survey areas. Values are thousand employed people aged 15 years and over.
notes: Annual Labour Force Survey employment, 2020–2025, for seven BC survey areas. Values are thousand employed people aged 15 years and over.

Healthcare and social assistance industry [62] and nursing and allied health occupations [313] overlap. They are alternative classifications and must not be added. Employment estimates are distinct from licensed nurse registrations.

North Coast and Nechako are one combined LFS reporting area. Statistics Canada’s 2025 guide confirms the 2021 geography; the map dissolves PGMaps ERs 5960 and 5970 into one polygon. Its value is shown once and never split. Original blank DGUID and ER-code fields remain blank; map_region_code is explicitly derived.
Exact source 2021 ER DGUIDs join native 2021 polygons. Select one classification and year before mapping; additional groups remain ambiguous rather than summed.

The seven display areas are disjoint reporting contexts. LFS target-population exclusions, including people living on reserves, still apply; coloured territory does not imply observations for every resident or location. Separate economic-region datasets retain their individual polygons.

datasets.title: Northern employer business locations
datasets.description: Employer business locations in seven Northern 2021 census municipalities, for selected industries. Locations are distinct from companies, employees, clinical sites and care capacity.
notes: Employer business locations in seven Northern 2021 census municipalities, for selected industries. Locations are distinct from companies, employees, clinical sites and care capacity.
The source excludes businesses without employees. Total industries and individual industries overlap and cannot be added.
Original REF_DATE is 2025-07, despite the archive’s December 2025 label. The release retains 19 reported municipality/industry combinations; two absent combinations are not invented or assigned zero.
Exact 2021 municipal DGUIDs join 2021 CSD polygons. Select one industry before mapping.

datasets.title: BC employer business locations
datasets.description: BC employer business locations by industry and employment-size category. The source excludes businesses without employees.
notes: BC employer business locations by industry and employment-size category. The source excludes businesses without employees.
Original REF_DATE is 2025-01, despite the archive’s June 2025 label. No current operating status is inferred.
Individual size categories and Total, with employees overlap and cannot be added together. Employer locations are distinct from employees, clinics and care capacity.
Province-only comparison; no Northern allocation or local point mapping.

datasets.title: BC industry hourly wages
datasets.description: BC annual hourly wages, 2020–2025: total gender, age 15 years and over, and full- and part-time employees together.
notes: BC annual hourly wages, 2020–2025: total gender, age 15 years and over, and full- and part-time employees together.
Average and median are alternative published statistics. Values are current nominal CAD per hour, without inflation adjustment.
Healthcare and social assistance is broader than clinical occupations. Provincial wages cannot be allocated to municipalities, hospitals or individual workers.

datasets.title: Canadian retirement age
datasets.description: Canadian annual average and median retirement ages among all retirees, 2015–2025. Total gender and total class of worker are selected explicitly.
notes: Canadian annual average and median retirement ages among all retirees, 2015–2025. Total gender and total class of worker are selected explicitly.
These are retrospective published ages, not retirement forecasts, Northern workforce attrition or occupation-specific staffing losses.

datasets.title: BC interprovincial migration
datasets.description: BC annual interprovincial migration from 2015/2016 onward. Arrivals and departures each sum the 12 other provinces and territories; net is calculated only when every flow is reported.
notes: BC annual interprovincial migration from 2015/2016 onward. Arrivals and departures each sum the 12 other provinces and territories; net is calculated only when every flow is reported.
Original annual migration intervals are retained. They are distinct from calendar-year employment and fiscal healthcare costs.
International migration, births, deaths and intraprovincial moves are absent. No Northern retention, local demand or future workforce forecast is inferred.

datasets.title: BC graduate employment income
datasets.description: BC graduation cohorts 2010–2017, four credentials, age 15–64, total gender, and Canadian and international students together. Only total field of study is present; no health-training subset is available.
notes: BC graduation cohorts 2010–2017, four credentials, age 15–64, total gender, and Canadian and international students together. Only total field of study is present; no health-training subset is available.
Published median employment income among graduates reporting income, measured two or five years after graduation, in 2022 constant CAD. A 2017 five-year outcome follows graduates to 2022.
Credentials and follow-up periods have different cohorts and denominators. Medians are never summed or averaged. No Northern campus, graduate retention or individual salary inference is made.

notes: CREA composite benchmark prices from the annual, not seasonally adjusted workbook, 2015–2025. April 2026 identifies the captured archive; the selected rows are complete annual periods.
A benchmark models a typical home. It is distinct from average sale prices, rents, dwelling stock and household affordability ratios. Values are nominal CAD.
Interior BC and provincial CREA markets do not correspond to Northern Health or municipal Census polygons. No Northern or Prince George prices are inferred.
Original workbook redistribution terms are not established. The Atlas releases a bounded, attributed factual extract and does not redistribute the source archives.

datasets.title: Vancouver construction price index
datasets.description: Archived quarterly construction price indexes for the Vancouver 2016 census metropolitan area, 2020 Q1–2024 Q2. The published base is 2017=100; values are indexes, not CAD.
notes: Archived quarterly construction price indexes for the Vancouver 2016 census metropolitan area, 2020 Q1–2024 Q2. The published base is 2017=100; values are indexes, not CAD.
Original YYYY-MM reference dates encode quarters. Residential and non-residential indexes are alternatives and cannot be added.
No Northern BC centres occur in this source. No city point, 2021 CSD join or current construction-cost forecast is inferred.

datasets.title: Canadian economic model inputs
datasets.description: Published 2022 Canadian input-output coefficients for hospitals, health-related services and scientific research. These are model inputs, not observed NHHR benefits or causal forecasts.
notes: Published 2022 Canadian input-output coefficients for hospitals, health-related services and scientific research. These are model inputs, not observed NHHR benefits or causal forecasts.
Direct, indirect, induced, simple and total coefficients overlap by definition. They cannot all be summed or transferred to Northern BC without a justified regional model and leakage assumptions.
Output coefficients are per dollar of industry output. No project cost is multiplied automatically and no return-on-investment claim is made.
